details.targetCommunity: Women residing at Dar-ul-Aman in Mandi Bahauddin
details.overview:
A safe shelter should protect the dignity, health and wellbeing of the women who live there. HRPF’s 2025 progress report describes its intervention at Dar-ul-Aman in Mandi Bahauddin after concerns were raised about the condition and management of the facility.

HRPF used a formal complaint and engagement with the Provincial Ombudsman Punjab to seek inspection, corrective action and stronger accountability. The report records improvements in sanitation and facility management following that intervention.
details.challenge:
The report describes poor sanitation and cleanliness, inadequate healthcare arrangements, weak oversight and deficiencies in monitoring. These conditions affected women living in a government shelter established to provide protection and rehabilitation.

The issue required an institutional response to the facilities and accountability concerns identified in the complaint.
details.approach:
HRPF brought the reported deficiencies to the attention of an oversight institution through a detailed complaint. The complaint called for urgent inspection, immediate rectification of deficiencies, administrative accountability and protection of residents’ rights.

Engagement with the Provincial Ombudsman’s office helped draw official attention to the shelter and initiate administrative inquiries and corrective measures.
objectives: Protect residents’ dignity and access to basic necessities.
Seek inspection and correction of sanitation and healthcare deficiencies.
activities: Gathered information about deficiencies at the shelter.
Submitted a detailed complaint to the Provincial Ombudsman Punjab.
Requested inspection, corrective measures and accountability.
Engaged with the oversight office about residents’ protection and facility conditions.
outcomes: The report records noticeable improvements in sanitation and facility management.

details.targetCommunity: Residents of Mianwal Ranjha using the local sanitation infrastructure
details.overview:
HRPF’s 2024 progress report documents the cleaning and repair of the sewerage scheme in Mianwal Ranjha in the public interest. The work addressed damaged pipes and roadside openings as part of efforts to improve local sanitation.

The report also records a separate request to the Drain Department Punjab to increase the capacity of the Fifth Drain. That request is distinct from the completed cleaning and repair work.
details.challenge:
Damaged sewerage pipes and the condition of roadside openings required attention to support public health and sanitation. The report identifies repair and cleaning of the existing scheme as the immediate work undertaken.

A request for greater drainage capacity was also submitted. The report does not provide technical measurements or confirm that the capacity expansion was completed.
details.approach:
The reported intervention focused on cleaning the existing scheme, repairing broken pipes and raising the level of roadside openings. A separate institutional request addressed the capacity of the Fifth Drain.

The completed repairs and the pending capacity request are presented separately so visitors can understand the reported outcome accurately.
objectives: Support public health and sanitation in Mianwal Ranjha.
Restore damaged parts of the existing sewerage scheme.
Raise the drainage-capacity concern with the relevant department.
activities: Cleaning of the local sewerage scheme.
Submission of a request to increase the Fifth Drain’s capacity.
outcomes: The report records completion of cleaning and repair work.
The drainage-capacity request was submitted; completion of an expansion is not established.

details.targetCommunity: Children and families seeking childhood vaccination in Mandi Bahauddin district
details.overview:
Childhood vaccination depends on families being able to access functioning public health services. HRPF’s 2022–2023 performance report describes difficulties accessing vaccination in Mandi Bahauddin district because of administrative issues at Basic Health Units and District Health Units.

HRPF visited the facilities and brought the issue to the Director General of Health Punjab. The report records a prompt response to improve the situation in the public interest.
details.challenge:
Administrative issues at Basic Health Units and District Health Units were making childhood vaccination difficult to access. The report describes a public-service access problem requiring attention from health authorities.

It does not identify the number of affected children, the facilities visited or a precise intervention date.
details.approach:
HRPF visited health facilities to understand the access difficulties and informed the Director General of Health Punjab. This approach linked observations at local facilities with the authority responsible for addressing the administrative concerns.

The report records action by the Director General to improve the situation. HRPF also recognised that response by presenting an honorary shield.
objectives: Raise difficulties in childhood vaccination access with health authorities.
Seek action on administrative problems affecting public health services.
Support children’s access to vaccination through institutional engagement.
activities: Visited Basic Health Units and District Health Units.
Informed the Director General of Health Punjab about vaccination-access difficulties.
Recorded the authority’s response in the performance report.
Presented an honorary shield in recognition of the Director General’s efforts.
outcomes: The vaccination-access concerns were brought to the Director General’s attention.
The report records a prompt response to improve the situation.
HRPF formally recognised the Director General’s efforts.
